screens.title: Sign in
screens.summary: Password authentication gates the workspace. This wireframe uses synthetic values and does not establish a session.

panels.title: Credentials
lines: Username: demo.reviewer
Password: hidden; show or hide control
Sign in is disabled while the request is pending.

panels.title: Field feedback
lines: Required fields retain stable labels.
A failed sign-in shows an error above the form.
Retry connection appears when a connection notice is present.

panels.title: Prototype navigation
lines: Sign in opens the signed-in wireframe only.
No credential is sent and no account is changed.

checks: Are field errors understandable and associated with the correct inputs?
Can a user distinguish incorrect credentials from an unavailable connection?
Does the pending state prevent duplicate submissions without losing the entered username?

transitions.label: Sign-in path
transitions.condition: Prototype navigation; the product requires successful authentication.

transitions.label: Connection retry
transitions.condition: A connection error or session-verification notice is visible.

screens.title: Comments
screens.summary: Browse retained publications independently from their delivery attempts and the investigation result.

panels.title: Search and filters
lines: Search publications: title, body, or number
Work item, delivery state, publication type, producer
More filters: exact Task ID and PR or issue number

panels.title: Directory behavior
lines: Apply updates the view; active filters can be removed individually.
Cursor pagination preserves the current query.
No comments and no matching comments are distinct states.

panels.title: Independent status
lines: A completed task does not establish successful comment delivery.
A publication can retain its previous body while delivery needs attention.

checks: Can a reviewer distinguish publication state from an individual delivery outcome?
Are exact Task ID filters visible, removable, and retained when returning from details?
Do loading, empty, filtered-empty, and refresh-error states explain the next useful action?

transitions.label: Refresh current directory
transitions.condition: No new delivery is submitted.

screens.title: Comment publication
screens.summary: Inspect the retained body, related work, and delivery history. The illustrated acknowledgement remains unconfirmed.

panels.title: Retained publication
lines: Type: review result for a sample pull request
Body: saved review summary and findings
Source, task, report, and GitHub links use the retained context.

panels.title: Delivery history
lines: Each attempt retains its original body and outcome.
Sending, succeeded, failed, cancelled, and unknown remain distinct.
An earlier delivered body can coexist with a newer uncertain request.

panels.title: Acknowledgement unknown
lines: Refresh publication reads the current object; it does not clear Unknown.
A new synchronization requires the exact preview and a separate confirmation.
This wireframe does not send, retry, or reconcile a real comment.

checks: Does the retained body make clear which content belongs to each attempt?
Does the unknown state avoid implying that refresh confirms or retries a submission?
Can the reviewer move to the exact source, task, and report without losing publication context?

transitions.label: Read current publication
transitions.condition: Unknown acknowledgement is retained.

screens.title: Webhook events
screens.summary: Trace incoming events through authorization, source import, task creation, and recovery.

panels.title: Filters
lines: Work item: all targets, pull requests, or issues
Handling state: accepted, source ready, processed, ignored, or failed
More filters: PR or issue number and static or E2E mode

panels.title: State meaning
lines: Processed describes event handling, not task completion.
Ignored is a recorded outcome with its own reason.
A failed event can have partial source or task context.

panels.title: Directory states
lines: Loading, no events, no matching events, and failed refresh need distinct feedback.
Additional filters remain visible as removable chips.

checks: Can the reviewer distinguish event handling from the linked task's execution state?
Are ignored events explained without presenting them as failures?
Are source number and task mode filters easy to discover on a narrow screen?

screens.title: Webhook event details
screens.summary: Keep the event outcome, failed phase, retained attempts, and related work visible before considering a recovery request.

panels.title: Recorded outcome
lines: Target: sample pull request; mode: static review
Failed phase: source import
A specific failure reason is shown independently from any task status.

panels.title: Handling timeline
lines: Authorization, source import, task creation, and recovery retain separate entries.
Retry scheduled, failed, ignored, and interrupted are distinct outcomes.
Event details retain delivery, repository, trigger, and receipt context.

panels.title: Recovery boundary
lines: Retry event opens a preview of the current event before confirmation.
Repository management and task-creation grants are required; E2E also requires execution access.
Refresh does not clear an unknown recovery acknowledgement.

checks: Does the failure explanation identify the exact phase and the next useful action?
Does recovery preview preserve the exact event and its current version?
Are related-work links shown only when their retained identities match this event?

transitions.label: Read current event
transitions.condition: This is not a recovery submission or an acknowledgement resolution.

transitions.label: Inspect linked task
transitions.condition: A task exists and matches this event's retained context.

transitions.label: Inspect linked report
transitions.condition: A matching report is available.

screens.title: Workers
screens.summary: Administrators inspect contact, capabilities, E2E admission, and resource ownership as separate signals.

panels.title: Worker detail
lines: Advertised and effective task capabilities remain distinct.
Repository assignments and static resource ownership have their own links.
Current E2E tasks and cleanup-pending attempts remain visible.

panels.title: Stop E2E work
lines: The product asks for confirmation before stopping E2E work.
New assignments stop; running work is cancelled and cleaned up.
Resources remain reserved until the worker confirms cleanup.

panels.title: Unconfirmed policy save
lines: Refresh workers, then review the latest saved policy before trying again.
No recent contact does not prove that owned resources are released.
This wireframe cannot confirm cleanup or resolve an unknown operation.

checks: Can an administrator distinguish admission policy, recent contact, and confirmed availability?
Does stopping E2E work explain cancellation and cleanup without implying immediate resource release?
Does an unconfirmed save require review of the latest policy instead of silently clearing uncertainty?

transitions.label: Read current worker snapshots
transitions.condition: No cleanup proof or operation result is synthesized.

screens.title: Repositories
screens.summary: The directory shows repositories in the signed-in user's scope and opens each repository's review and automation settings.

panels.title: Repository overview
lines: Review work: pull requests, issues, tasks, comments, and webhook events
Automation: event intake and automatic reply summaries
Import work item and Open on GitHub are separate entry points.

panels.title: Directory search
lines: Find a repository by name or ID.
No scope, no matching repositories, and unavailable repository links have distinct states.
Intake and reply summaries can fail independently.

panels.title: Workspace scheduling
lines: Scheduling applies to all repositories.
It opens a separate workspace-level view rather than a repository-specific limit.

checks: Is the difference between repository settings and workspace scheduling apparent?
Can users with read-only scope understand why management controls are unavailable?
Do partial summary failures preserve access to the repository's remaining information?

screens.title: Repository intake
screens.summary: Configure assignment and trusted E2E command intake. The illustrated local draft has unsaved changes.

panels.title: Event intake
lines: Listen for assignments: on
Allow trusted E2E commands: off
Assignment recipient ID: sample GitHub user ID

panels.title: Trusted actors and endpoint
lines: Trusted GitHub user IDs: sample allowlist
Webhook endpoint: read-only value with copy control
Field errors identify the precise invalid value.

panels.title: Save behavior
lines: Save settings requires repository management access and a net change.
Busy or conflicting settings disable editing and submission.
Discard, Download draft, and Reload have different effects.

checks: Are assignment intake and trusted E2E command intake explained as independent controls?
Are invalid IDs and missing permissions explained next to the relevant fields?
Can a reviewer distinguish saving, discarding, downloading, and reloading a draft?

transitions.label: Inspect a conflicting save response
transitions.condition: Scenario navigation only; no setting is submitted.

transitions.label: Attempt to leave a dirty form
Open reply settings
transitions.condition: The product invokes the unsaved-change guard when the intake draft is dirty.

transitions.label: Return to directory
transitions.condition: The product invokes the unsaved-change guard when the intake draft is dirty.

screens.title: Repository replies
screens.summary: Edit future automatic replies using required placeholders and a template preview before saving.

panels.title: Automatic replies
lines: Automatic investigation replies: on
Assignment progress comments: on
Enabling replies can require a separate authorization confirmation.

panels.title: Template editor
lines: Template: PR result
Required placeholders: identity, conclusion, summary, findings, details
Other templates: issue result, received, started, failed, and completed

panels.title: Preview and activity
lines: Preview renders the selected template without posting a comment.
Save affects future replies; existing delivery state stays separate.
Recent reply activity links to retained publications and tasks.

checks: Are required placeholders and their ordering understandable before an invalid save?
Is preview clearly separated from authorizing or publishing future automatic comments?
Can users distinguish the current template configuration from earlier delivery outcomes?

transitions.label: Inspect preview boundary
transitions.condition: This static wireframe does not render or submit a template.

transitions.label: Return to directory
transitions.condition: Dirty template edits invoke the navigation guard in the product.

screens.title: Workspace scheduling
screens.summary: Inspect global static concurrency, E2E capacity, and resource owners across all repositories.

panels.title: Static concurrency
lines: Occupied static slots: illustrated usage of the saved limit
Maximum concurrent static investigations: editable numeric field
Save requires administrator access, valid input, and a net change.

panels.title: E2E capacity
lines: Worker availability and effective task support determine capacity.
Pending cleanup remains visible independently of admission policy.
Stopping or unresponsive workers do not imply released resources.

panels.title: Current resource owners
lines: Task, attempt, worker, lease state, and acquisition time
Held and needs-cleanup leases remain listed.
Task links open the corresponding investigation context.

checks: Is the workspace-wide scope visible before changing static concurrency?
Can operators explain why a resource remains occupied after cancellation?
Are save errors, stale configuration, and unchanged values represented separately?

transitions.label: Review unsaved-change behavior
transitions.condition: A local concurrency draft differs from the saved value.

screens.title: Accounts
screens.summary: Administrators manage account identity, repository scope, permissions, and action capabilities.

panels.title: Directory controls
lines: Search by name or username.
Filter All, Enabled, or Disabled.
Create account and account editing open dialogs.

panels.title: Access model
lines: Administrator status and repository scope are separate.
Permissions, action capabilities, and repository execution access remain explicit.
An enabled account does not automatically have every action grant.

panels.title: Directory states
lines: Non-administrators see an access-required state.
Loading, no accounts, no matching accounts, and refresh errors are distinct.

checks: Does the directory communicate effective access without conflating enabled and administrator status?
Are repository scope and action grants discoverable before opening an account?
Is the difference between managing another account and changing one's own password clear?

screens.title: Account editor dialog
screens.summary: A modal editor separates identity, repository access, capabilities, and credential reset. This wireframe changes no account.

panels.title: Identity
lines: Username: demo.reviewer; display name: Demo reviewer
Initial password is present only when creating an account.
Administrator and Account enabled are separate switches.

panels.title: Repository access
lines: Repository IDs define the allowed scope.
Permissions include management, task creation, cancellation, preparation, and execution.
Action capabilities and repository code execution are separate grants.

panels.title: Conflict and reset
lines: A conflicting version requires reading and reviewing the latest account.
Reset password uses its own dialog and confirms sign-out everywhere.
Closing a dirty editor invokes the unsaved-change guard.

checks: Can an administrator distinguish preparing an action from executing it?
Does the version-conflict flow preserve the local draft until the latest access is reviewed?
Does a password reset explain session invalidation and require explicit acknowledgement?

transitions.label: Return to account directory
transitions.condition: Dirty edits are guarded in the product; this link only changes the wireframe.

transitions.label: Inspect post-reset sign-in
transitions.condition: Scenario navigation only; no password reset is performed.

screens.title: My account
screens.summary: Inspect the current identity and grants, or change the account password using a dedicated form.

panels.title: Current account
lines: Display name: Demo reviewer; username: demo.reviewer
Repository scope and effective permissions are shown read-only.
Administrator status is shown only when granted.

panels.title: Change password
lines: Current password: hidden
New password: hidden; confirm new password: hidden
Each password field supports show or hide and field-specific feedback.

panels.title: Session behavior
lines: Changing a password ends existing sessions and requires sign-in again.
Unsaved password fields invoke the navigation guard.
This prototype uses no real credentials and changes no password.

checks: Are current, new, and confirmation password fields unambiguous?
Does the form explain that a successful change requires signing in again?
Are password validation errors and unsaved-field protection understandable without exposing values?

transitions.label: Inspect post-change sign-in
transitions.condition: Scenario navigation only; no password change is performed.

transitions.label: Attempt to leave entered password fields
Return to the workspace
transitions.condition: The product guards any dirty password form.

screens.title: Session expired
screens.summary: An expired or unverifiable session replaces the workspace with sign-in and clears identity-bound cached data.

panels.title: Session notice
lines: Your session expired. Sign in again.
An unavailable session check offers connection retry or a new sign-in.

panels.title: Identity boundary
lines: Investigation requests are suspended while access is unverified.
Queries and cached private data are cleared when identity or grants change.
Access is resumed only after a valid authenticated session is established.

panels.title: Return path
lines: The sign-in form is displayed over the current route.
A valid new identity must still be authorized for the requested view.
The prototype does not restore or impersonate a real session.

checks: Does the notice distinguish expiry from failure to verify the current connection?
Is private workspace content removed while the session is unverified?
Does re-entry respect the new identity's scope instead of restoring unauthorized cached content?

transitions.label: Retry session verification
transitions.condition: The wireframe makes no success claim and leaves the gate visible.

screens.title: Discard unsaved changes?
screens.summary: Leaving a dirty form requires a choice. An in-progress operation instead keeps navigation blocked until its result is available.

panels.title: Dirty draft
lines: Your unsaved edits will be lost.
Submitted requests and their saved outcomes remain available.
Keep editing preserves the current local form.

panels.title: Busy variant
lines: Title: An operation is still in progress
Wait for its result before leaving this view.
Discard is unavailable while an active operation is busy.

panels.title: Prototype example
lines: This example starts in Repository intake.
Discard changes opens the repository directory wireframe.
No actual draft, request, or server operation is removed.

checks: Does the dialog identify the affected draft and the consequence of leaving?
Is discarding local text clearly separated from cancelling or undoing a submitted request?
Does the busy variant prevent navigation without suggesting the operation has failed?

transitions.label: Keep the intake draft
transitions.condition: The example's originating view is Repository intake.

transitions.label: Continue to the chosen destination
transitions.condition: Discard affects local draft state only and is unavailable while busy.

screens.title: Repository settings changed
screens.summary: A version conflict keeps the local settings draft visible and disables saving until the latest saved settings are loaded.

panels.title: Conflict notice
lines: Settings changed. Your draft is kept.
Reload saved settings to replace the draft with the latest version.
Make the intended changes again after reviewing the new values.

panels.title: Available choices
lines: Download draft preserves a local reference to the current edits.
Reload uses the navigation guard before replacing dirty values.
There is no silent overwrite or automatic field merge.

panels.title: Review boundary
lines: This screen illustrates a possible response to a save attempt.
The wireframe has not submitted a save or detected a live conflict.
Account conflicts use a separate latest-version review flow.

checks: Is it clear that the current local draft is retained but cannot overwrite a newer version?
Does Reload explain that it replaces the local draft instead of merging changes?
Can the reviewer preserve the draft before choosing to load the latest settings?

transitions.label: Review draft-replacement guard
transitions.condition: This generic guard example does not complete Reload.

transitions.label: Inspect the intake form
transitions.condition: Scene navigation does not resolve the illustrated conflict.

journeys.title: Enter the workspace and recover an expired session
journeys.summary: Review the authentication gate, signed-in navigation, account controls, and identity boundaries without using real credentials.

steps.label: Sign in
steps.note: Inspect required fields, password visibility, pending feedback, and connection retry.

steps.label: Enter review work
steps.note: A successful product login reveals only the repository scope and actions granted to that identity.

steps.label: Inspect current account
steps.note: Review access and the separate password-change flow.

steps.label: Handle expiry
steps.note: Suspend requests, clear identity-bound cached data, and show the sign-in gate.

steps.label: Re-enter
steps.note: A new valid session must re-establish its own permissions; this prototype does not authenticate.

branches.label: Invalid fields or unavailable connection retain the sign-in form.
Entered password values are protected when leaving.
A successful password change requires signing in again in the product.
An unverified connection keeps the authentication gate visible.

journeys.title: Review repository settings, local drafts, and version conflicts
journeys.summary: Trace repository configuration separately from all-repository scheduling and inspect the consequences of leaving or reloading a local draft.

steps.label: Choose repository scope
steps.note: Locate a configured repository and inspect independent intake and reply summaries.

steps.label: Edit intake
steps.note: Review assignment intake, trusted E2E commands, actor IDs, and permission-gated saving.

steps.label: Attempt to leave
steps.note: Keep editing or discard local changes; busy requests have a separate guarded state.

steps.label: Keep editing
steps.note: The illustrated intake draft remains the review context.

steps.label: Inspect a conflicting save
steps.note: The draft is kept, save is blocked, and Reload replaces local values after the guard.

steps.label: Review automatic replies
steps.note: Inspect template validation, preview, authorization, and links to existing publications.

branches.label: Discard the illustrated local draft and continue to the directory.
Reload of dirty settings requires draft-replacement confirmation.
Open global capacity configuration for all repositories.
Inspect worker contact, admission, and pending cleanup.
Review existing delivery activity separately from future templates.

journeys.title: Trace an event through investigation and publication activity
journeys.summary: Keep webhook handling, task execution, report content, and comment delivery as separate outcomes with explicit context links.

steps.label: Find an incoming event
steps.note: Filter by target, handling state, number, or task mode.

steps.label: Inspect handling
steps.note: Read the exact phase, retained timeline, and related work; a failed import may have no task.

steps.label: Follow matching task context
steps.note: This branch applies only when a task exists and matches the event identity.

steps.label: Read saved conclusions
steps.note: Task completion and report findings do not establish publication success.

steps.label: Find outgoing publication
steps.note: Use exact Task ID filtering to locate the producer's retained publication.

steps.label: Inspect delivery and retained body
steps.note: Unknown acknowledgement stays unresolved; refreshing is not a resend or confirmation.

branches.label: Review intake settings when handling was prevented by configuration.
Refresh reads the event without resolving an unknown recovery request.
Refresh retains the illustrated unconfirmed acknowledgement.
Return to the producer task without changing delivery state.
